answer: An AI agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with stake-weighted identity: an agent locks collateral before its vote or work counts. Influence scales with locked stake, not with the number of names an attacker invents, so splitting a fixed budget among thousands of fakes buys no extra power, and misbehavior triggers slashing that seizes the stake. Picture the registry as an atlas of marble slabs bolted to a ledge: to stand there the attacker pays for every slab. Dominating the system costs the stake needed to outvote honest agents, making mass identity fabrication economically futile.
